title: Finding what was said in an old recording
description: Searching the archive and opening the specific fragments the search result rests on.

blocks.text: A person remembers the topic of a conversation but not the date or the file name. The search offers matching fragments, shows the surrounding text and opens the audio at the right spot. A short answer drawn from the archive stays an index, not a replacement for the source.

quote.text: its file management is terrible. If you have a lot of notes and recordings it starts to glitch and the search feature is flawed.

blocks.text: An answer that takes you to the recording

You could start with search across names and a checked transcript within one collection. Failed recognition has to be taken into account: the absence of a match does not prove that the topic was never discussed.
Search whose basis you can check

The idea is worth testing on an archive that has already built up, where searching genuinely takes time. Across a few recent notes an elaborate dialogue with the archive may give no advantage over a clear list and ordinary search.
